title: Service trajectory stabilization — 90-day compact
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a compact, cross-functional 90-day plan to pull struggling services into a predictable stability trajectory. Treat services as trajectories (improving / flat / degrading) — not static labels. The goal is to reduce fire frequency, lower P99 latency spikes, and get at least 80% of production-facing services into a monitored SLO tier with a playbook and owner.

Audience:
Platform eng, SRE, serving-runtime, infra, product owners for feature teams, solutions engineering. Quick-read for managers; operational checklist for on-call and pairing.

Outcome commitments (90 days):
- SLO coverage: 80% of targeted services have a defined SLO in the catalog (availability or latency as appropriate).
- Observability: Each targeted service has a lightweight telemetry dashboard + one automated alert linked to an incident runbook.
- Error budget cadence: 100% of services with SLOs added to weekly error-budget review rotation for the first 6 weeks, then biweekly.
- Stabilization experiments: Launch 3 cross-team experiments (batching tweaks, KV cache warmups, adaptive batching) and measure token-cost vs P95/P99 impact.
- Handoff: Every stabilized service completes a handoff checklist and a short owner-runbook entry in the platform repo.

Scope (what we will target first):
- Priority: production services with >10% customer impact score or >3 incidents in last 90 days.
- Start batch (15 services): mix of hosted-api routes, embedded-embedding pipeline, and one private-deploy customer endpoint.
- Exclusions: early-stage experimental features, internal-only tooling (unless incident-prone).

High-level phases and timeline (90 days)
- Week 0 (Prep): intake, triage, and pairings assigned. Kickoff: share service-trajectory canvas, collect ownership, baseline telemetry.
- Weeks 1–3 (Discovery + Quick Instrumentation): deepen metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, queue depth, cache hit rate). Add one golden metric and one alert.
- Weeks 4–6 (SLO design + Policy): set SLO target, error budget burn policy, gating rules for rollouts (canary thresholds). Draft runbook.
- Weeks 7–10 (Stabilization experiments): run 3 experiments per service cohort (tunable config changes / routing policy / batching / fallback model). Compare cost delta and quality metrics.
- Weeks 11–12 (Handoff and cadence): finalize runbooks, roll into error-budget cadence, place owners on the rotation. Retro and next-sprint backlog.

Daily/Weekly cadence (suggested):
- Weekly sync (30 min): platform + one product/feature rep for the cohort. Share blockers, experiment outcomes, decisions.
- Biweekly error-budget review (60 min): review top 10 burn cases, approve mitigations or rollback policies.
- Monthly stakeholder briefing (20 min): exec summary (SLO coverage, major stability wins, remaining high-risk services).

Roles and responsibilities (high level):
- Platform-engineering (lead): run intake, maintain SLO catalog, own telemetry templates and automation.
- SRE: run incident/replay analysis, own runbook quality checks, facilitate oncall rotations for error budgets.
- Serving-runtime / infra: implement configuration experiments (batching, KV caching), provide perf measurements.
- Product/Feature owner: prioritize remediation work, accept SLOs and rollback policies.
- Solutions eng / CS (customer-facing endpoints): coordinate private-deploy handoffs and compliance checks.

Concrete deliverables (artifact list):
- Service Trajectory Canvas (one per service) — minimal fields: owner, golden metric, current trajectory, incident history, proposed mitigations.
- SLO entry in catalog (YAML/metadata) with target, rationale, and linked runbook.
- Lightweight runbook template filled (playbook + quick mitigations + triage checklist).
- Experiment diary (short bullets + metric snapshots) per experiment.
- Handoff checklist completed and PR merged to platform repo.

Stabilization experiment examples (templates):
- Adaptive batching: increase batch wait time by 20ms for low-QPS routes, measure P95/P99 and token cost.
- Prefix caching: enable prefix/KV cache for hot prefixes, track cache hit rate and downstream latency.
- Canary fallback policy: route 10% of traffic to lower-cost quantized model during peak and monitor QA regressions.

Success metrics (how we measure):
- SLO coverage percentage (target 80%).
- Mean weekly incident count for cohort (target -40% from baseline).
- P99 latency improvement for targeted routes (relative target vary by service; aim for 10–30% improvement for 50% of cohort).
- Cost per 1k requests delta for experiments (report tradeoffs).
- Time-to-handoff (PR merged to platform repo within 2 weeks of stabilization).

Runbook/handoff template (checklist):
- Owner and secondary owner listed in catalog.
- Golden metric + alert bound defined.
- Playbook: 3-step triage + immediate mitigation.
- Experiment history: last 3 experiments with results and decisions.
- Dependencies noted (upstream models, external APIs, infra features).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Experiment causes user-visible quality regression. Mitigation: start experiments at 1–5% traffic, have automatic rollback on quality metric drop >X.
- Risk: Teams lack capacity to implement instrumentation. Mitigation: platform to provide templated dashboards and a pairing hour offering.
- Risk: SLOs set too tight and cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: adopt conservative initial targets and iterate with product.

Dependencies and blockers to call out now:
- Observability gaps: services missing request-level tracing or consistent latency buckets. (ACTION: infra telemetry sprint to add for cohort).
- Capacity: serving-runtime needs a 2-week dev window to run adaptive-batching code paths for 4 services. (OWNER: Miguel).
- Compliance check for private-deploy service (customer X): legal sign-off required for audit logs. (OWNER: Priya).

Immediate next actions (first two weeks):
- Week 0: Intake spreadsheet populated (owner: Lena). Link: ENG-4521.
- Book platform <> SRE pairing hours for the 15-service cohort (Miguel).
- Push telemetry dashboard template PR (PR#7890) and share in slack:#reliability-ops (Ava).
- Schedule kickoff — 2026-10-14 10:00 PT (send invites).

Open questions / discussion items:
- What is an acceptable initial error-budget policy for private-deploy customers? (legal + CS input required).
- Should we include non-prod environments in trajectory assessments (benefit: faster experiment cycles vs noise)?
- How do we tie quality monitoring (model output regressions) into SLO dashboards effectively? Proposal: a separate "quality signal" tied to evaluation prompts for each model route.

Notes to self / working reminders:
- Keep canvas intentionally lightweight — this is an accelerator, not a heavyweight program office.
- Use heuristics for initial SLO tiers; revisit after 6 weeks of data.
- Make all artifacts PR-based so product owners can review and sign-off in a single workflow.

If you’re reading this and want to join the initial cohort pairing: ping me (Lena) or drop a note in slack:#reliability-ops. We’ll triage capacity and put a small badge on high-impact services first.
